title: Real Madrid Player Ratings vs. Roma: Youngsters Rescue Jose Mourinho in Vintage Comeback
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto CasillasOct 14, 2026Substitutes Arda Güler (left) and Endrick had three goal involvements combined in the last 10 minutes.  / Filippo Monteforte/AFP/Getty ImagesReal Madrid overcame a two-goal deficit inside the last 10 minutes of the game to defeat Roma 4–3 in a simply remarkable, trademark Champions League comeback on Wednesday night.

Roma were on the front foot from the start, taking the game to a visiting Real Madrid side that looked outclassed in terms of energy, intensity and aggressiveness. After a couple of brilliant Thibaut Courtois saves, the hosts finally went ahead thanks to a long distance Marten de Roon strike that took a slight deflection 20 minutes in.

Donyell Malen was inches away from doubling the lead minutes later, but when Real Madrid looked at their worst, a poor clearance attempt left the ball bouncing for Kylian Mbappé to fire a rocket from distance to equalize just five minutes later.

But Los Blancos never looked like the better side, and they crumbled in the first 15 minutes of the second half. A costly Vinícius Júnior turnover led to Malen restoring Roma’s lead and then he bagged his brace with a calm finish that was initially waved off for offside.

Then came Jose Mourinho’s substitutions that completely changed the game. The introduction of Endrick and Carlos Espí revitalized Madrid’s attack, and inside the final 10 minutes, the pair scored in a matter of seconds to equalize. In stoppage time, it was Antonio Rüdiger who won from a corner to complete a simply incredible Real Madrid comeback.

In arguably the best game of the young season, Real Madrid pulled off a historic comeback to make it two wins on the bounce to start their Champions League campaign. The performance for much of the game was beyond worrying, but the 15-time European champions showed they’re still capable of producing miracles out of nowhere in their favorite competition.

Federico Valverde struggled significantly against Roma.  / Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Ciancaphoto Studio/Getty Images At what point will Real Madrid finally give up on deploying an Aurélien Tchouaméni–Federico Valverde midfield double pivot? There is plenty of evidence that suggests it just doesn’t work, and the midfield duo was once again lackluster on Wednesday night.

Make no mistake, Tchouaméni and Valverde are good players, but they don’t work together as a pairing. Neither is capable of controlling game through their passing, nor disciplined enough positionally to avoid Madrid from playing basketball games defined by transitions.

Against a Roma side that aggressively man-marks, having two midfielders that aren’t exactly press-resistant led to dangerous turnovers in build up. Halfway through the first half, Courtois and Madrid’s defenders opted to stop looking for their midfield duo and instead lobbed long balls up the pitch for the forwards to win. The midfield pairing finished the first half with just 33 completed passes combined—Courtois had more accurate passes (19) than Tchouaméni (17) and Valverde (16).

Real Madrid are simply unable to control games with this midfield duo. They also clearly lack an organizer capable of resisting press and conducting possessions from deep, something Bernardo Silva might be able to offer if Mourinho didn’t seem uninterested in giving him significant minutes.

There’s plenty of issues Real Madrid must fix, but it’s incredibly puzzling that as managers come and go, Valverde and Tchouaméni continue to start together in midfield. It’s an indictment on the club’s recruitment, but it’s also on the manager to change something that’s clearly not working.
As a consequence of Madrid’s uninspiring double pivot, Roma were the better team for much of the night, looking unthreatened defensively and capable of creating danger at any given moment.
Antonio Rüdiger (bottom) won the game for Real Madrid at the death.  / Paolo Bruno/Getty Images *Ratings Provided by FotMob*

GK: Thibaut Courtois—6.4: The five-minute mark still hadn’t arrived, and Courtois had already produced two magnificent saves to deny the hosts from taking an early lead. Despite conceding three, he was vital in keeping his team in the game.

RB: Denzel Dumfries—5.7: Undisciplined in his marking of Paulo Dybala all game, allowing the Argentine time and space to manufacture Roma’s attacks. Caught out of position routinely in a dreadful evening for the Dutchman.
CB: Ibrahima Konaté—6.2: After a solid start he was completely dominated by Malen in the second half.
CB: Antonio Rüdiger—7.4: Tried to jump forward to intercept passes and left plenty of open space behind him routinely. Nevertheless, all of it will be forgotten after he scored the dramatic winner.
LB: Marc Cucurella—6.3: Characteristically stout defensively but missed the clearest chance of the night, alone against the goalkeeper but dragging his shot wide.

DM: Federico Valverde—7.2: Spent much of the game just jogging around the middle of the park without making any notable contributions. His bursts of speed to try to win possession back high up the pitch were unsuccessful and left Los Blancos exposed in midfield.
